set1.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set1.q: How is scaling described?
opts: Thickening and hardening of the skin
That is lichenification.
Accumulation of loose or adherent cornified fragments of the epidermis, typically grey or white
Correct.
A dried crust of serum
That is serum crusting.
A scratch or abrasion in which the top layer of the skin is worn away by repeated rubbing or friction
That is an excoriation.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which test should be considered before starting substantial compression for stasis dermatitis?
opts: A punch biopsy of the affected gaiter skin
Biopsy is not part of the routine stasis dermatitis workup.
A bacterial culture taken from the affected skin
That would only address suspected secondary infection.
An ankle-brachial index or toe pressure
Correct — arterial status has to be clarified first, because compression on an ischaemic limb causes harm.
A venous duplex ultrasound of the affected leg
That is ordered when reflux, obstruction or thrombosis is suspected.

set1.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set1.q: What is lichenification?
opts: Accumulation of loose cornified fragments of the epidermis
That is scaling.
A break in the skin
That is a fissure.
Abnormal formation of connective tissue
That is a scar.
Thickening and hardening of the skin
Correct — it develops from chronic rubbing or scratching.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which education points are named for atopic dermatitis?
opts: Apply emollient after rinsing, avoid irritants, use fragrance-free skincare, demonstrate quantity and application, and give a written flare and infection action plan
Correct — corticosteroid concerns are addressed directly rather than avoided.
Bathe as little as possible, avoid all moisturisers, use only prescription cleansers, and stop any topical steroid at the first sign of improvement
Overbathing is a risk factor but emollients are foundational.
Apply the strongest available steroid at the first sign of a flare, then stop abruptly
Potency is chosen by site, and application is demonstrated rather than maximised.
Avoid all sun exposure and apply broad-spectrum sunscreen several times daily
That is photoprotection advice from Lecture 3.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the foundation of treatment for diaper dermatitis?
opts: A high-potency topical corticosteroid until resolution
Only a brief course of a low-potency steroid is used, under guidance.
Reducing moisture and irritant exposure through frequent changes, gentle cleansing, air exposure and superabsorbent diapers, with a thick zinc oxide or petrolatum barrier at each change
Correct. The previous barrier layer need not be scrubbed away if it remains clean.
A topical antifungal applied at every diaper change regardless of cause, together with a course of oral antibiotics to prevent secondary bacterial infection of the damaged barrier
Antifungals are added when candidal disease is suspected or confirmed.
Oral antibiotics to prevent secondary infection
Antibiotics are used only when bacterial infection is clinically supported.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which topical corticosteroid is classified as mild?
opts: Clobetasol propionate 0.05%
That is the high potency agent.
Hydrocortisone, at all strengths
Correct — 0.1%, 0.5%, 1% and 2.5% all sit in the mild tier.
Triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%
That is in the medium to high tier.
Betamethasone valerate 0.1%
That is in the medium to high tier.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the herald patch, and how often does it occur?
opts: A coin-shaped plaque occurring in half of cases
That describes nummular eczema.
A single 2 to 5 cm round or oval, sharply demarcated pink or salmon plaque on the chest, neck or back, occurring in 50 to 90% of cases
Correct — it precedes the general eruption by one to two weeks.
A raindrop-shaped papule occurring in every case
That describes guttate psoriasis.
A single tense bulla on the trunk, occurring in about a third of cases before the wider eruption appears elsewhere
That describes bullous pemphigoid.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How does first-line treatment of alopecia areata differ between children and adults?
opts: Oral minoxidil first line in children; oral finasteride first line in adults
Those are treatments for androgenetic alopecia.
Phototherapy first line in children; systemic immunosuppression first line in adults
Neither is described as first line here.
Topical steroids first line in children ten and under; intralesional steroids first line in adolescents and adults
Correct — injections are avoided in young children.
Intralesional steroids first line in children ten and under; topical steroids first line in adults
That reverses the two.

set1.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set1.q: A fluid-filled lesion greater than one centimetre is called what?
opts: A nodule
A nodule is solid rather than fluid-filled.
A bulla
Correct — a vesicle is the same lesion up to one centimetre.
A vesicle
A vesicle is up to one centimetre.
A pustule
A pustule is defined by its leukocyte content.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which scale classifies skin type by its response to ultraviolet light?
opts: The Fitzpatrick scale
Correct — six types, from always burns and never tans through to never burns.
The SCORTEN score
That estimates mortality in toxic epidermal necrolysis.
The Auspitz sign
That is a physical finding in psoriasis, not a scale.
The Nikolsky sign
That is a physical finding in blistering disease, not a scale.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which medications can produce lichenoid reactions?
opts: Statins and proton pump inhibitors
These are not the named agents.
Topical corticosteroids
Those are associated with perioral dermatitis rather than lichenoid reactions.
Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, hydrochlorothiazide, quinidine and some beta blockers
Correct — worth asking about, since the eruption can mimic idiopathic lichen planus.
Penicillins, cephalosporins and the macrolide antibiotics, taken either together as a class or individually
These are not the named agents.

set1.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set1.q: How is a poorly demarcated lesion described?
opts: Irregular or blotchy in appearance, without well-defined borders
Correct — as against a well demarcated lesion, which has clearly defined borders.
Smaller than one centimetre in every dimension measured
Demarcation is about border definition rather than size.
Present in more than one body region
That is distribution.
Raised above the surrounding skin surface
That is elevation, part of primary morphology.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How does treatment of allergic contact dermatitis change when the eruption is extensive rather than limited?
opts: A more potent topical corticosteroid is applied to a larger surface area instead
Extensive disease moves to systemic therapy rather than more topical.
An oral antibiotic is added, since extensive disease is usually secondarily infected
Antibiotics are not the described escalation here.
Phototherapy is started three times weekly over a five-week course
That is not the described escalation for this condition.
High-dose oral corticosteroids replace the high-potency topical steroid used for limited disease
Correct — soothing measures such as oatmeal baths and cool compresses are used throughout.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is first-line treatment for alopecia areata by age group?
opts: Oral finasteride in adults and topical minoxidil in children under the age of ten years
Finasteride is for male-pattern hair loss.
Systemic corticosteroids in all age groups
Intralesional and topical routes are specified rather than systemic.
Intralesional steroids in adolescents and adults; topical steroids in children aged ten and under
Correct, and psychological support is named as one of the most important considerations.
Topical minoxidil at every age
Minoxidil is used for androgenetic alopecia.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which androgen is chiefly responsible for male-pattern hair loss?
opts: Dihydrotestosterone
Correct — male-pattern hair loss is an androgen-dependent trait with a strong paternal influence on risk.
Testosterone acting directly on the follicle
Dihydrotestosterone is the androgen named.
Oestradiol
This is not the androgen responsible.
Cortisol
This is not implicated in androgenetic alopecia.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which hand-care advice is given for dyshidrotic eczema?
opts: Wash the hands as infrequently as possible and avoid all emollients, since they trap the vesicles
Emollients are applied as often as possible.
Wear occlusive gloves continuously, including overnight and during sleep
Cotton gloves over heavy emollient at night belong to irritant contact dermatitis.
Lukewarm water and soap-free cleansers, dry thoroughly, then emollient immediately and as often as possible
Correct, alongside avoiding detergents, solvents, hair lotions or dyes, and acidic foods.
Hot water with an antibacterial soap, air dry, then a light lotion once daily
Hot water and harsh soap worsen the barrier dysfunction.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the prognosis of atopic dermatitis?
opts: Steadily progressive, with universal involvement by adulthood
Many patients improve as they get older.
Curable with a single course of a potent topical corticosteroid
The condition is controlled rather than cured.
Chronic and relapsing, but many patients improve with age
Correct — it may improve, persist or recur.
Self-limiting over six to eight weeks with no recurrence
That is the course of pityriasis rosea.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How is mild perioral dermatitis treated once the corticosteroid is stopped?
opts: A higher-potency topical corticosteroid applied twice daily
Continued corticosteroid exposure perpetuates the condition.
Topical ketoconazole
Antifungals are the mainstay of seborrhoeic dermatitis rather than this.
Oral prednisone
Systemic steroids are not the treatment described.
Topical metronidazole, erythromycin, pimecrolimus or azelaic acid
Correct, with oral tetracycline or doxycycline for more extensive or persistent disease.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is a Tzanck smear used for, and what is preferred for confirmation?
opts: Rapid detection of fungal elements in skin, hair or nail, with fungal culture preferred for confirmation of the species
That describes potassium hydroxide preparation and fungal culture.
Detection of the scabies mite, with dermoscopy preferred for confirmation
That describes mineral oil testing.
Detection of immune deposits, with serum ELISA preferred for confirmation
That describes direct immunofluorescence.
Rapid evaluation of vesicular lesions for herpesvirus cytologic changes, with polymerase chain reaction preferred for confirmation
Correct — the smear is fast, the polymerase chain reaction is definitive.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What does light microscopy show in bullous pemphigoid?
opts: Granular immunoglobulin A deposited at the tips of the dermal papillae
That is dermatitis herpetiformis, in Lecture 3.
Neutrophils aligned in a straight narrow row at the dermal-epidermal junction
Correct — a distinctive pattern at the level where the split occurs.
Acantholytic keratinocytes separated from one another within the epidermis
That is the pemphigus finding.
A band-like infiltrate of lymphocytes filling the papillary dermis
That is the lichen planus finding.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What is the mainstay of treatment for seborrhoeic dermatitis?
opts: Topical antifungals such as ketoconazole, with steroids used early to reduce inflammation
Correct. Scalp disease uses ketoconazole or selenium sulfide shampoo; facial disease uses ketoconazole cream or lotion.
High-potency topical corticosteroids alone, continued long term as monotherapy
Steroids are adjunctive and used early; antifungals are the mainstay.
Oral terbinafine
Topical antifungals are the mainstay for this condition.
Oral doxycycline
Tetracyclines are used for perioral dermatitis rather than this.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How does the timing of irritant contact dermatitis vary with the irritant?
opts: Mild irritants such as soaps may progress over weeks, while alkalis and acids may present within minutes or be delayed up to 24 hours or more
Correct — the agent determines the tempo.
All irritants produce symptoms within minutes of exposure
Mild irritants can take weeks.
All irritants produce symptoms 48 to 72 hours after exposure regardless of whether the agent is a mild soap or a concentrated acid
That timing belongs to delayed hypersensitivity in the allergic form.
Timing does not vary with the irritant
The lecture states it varies by exposure.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What characterises pustular psoriasis of the Von Zumbusch type?
opts: A slowly progressive eruption of silvery scaling plaques developing over many months on the extensor surfaces of the elbows and knees, without fever, chills, malaise or any systemic upset at all
That describes plaque psoriasis.
Raindrop papules following streptococcal infection
That is guttate psoriasis.
Joint pain with sausage digits and nail pitting
That is psoriatic arthritis.

Abrupt, life-threatening onset with several days of fever then a generalised eruption of 2 to 3 mm pustules over trunk and extremities including nail beds, palms and soles, which may form lakes of pus
Correct, and it may follow systemic steroid withdrawal. It is commonly mistaken for bacterial or viral infection.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What determines whether lichen simplex chronicus recurs?
opts: Whether the initiating itch is controlled, since recurrence is common if it is not
Correct — sleep, anxiety, neuropathic symptoms and the primary dermatosis all need addressing.
Whether the plaque was biopsied before treatment was started
Biopsy is diagnostic rather than a determinant of recurrence.
Whether a superpotent rather than a potent steroid was used
A potent steroid for a limited course is what is described.
Whether the patient was over sixty years of age at the first presentation
Age is not the stated determinant.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which test is ordered in nummular eczema when tinea corporis cannot be ruled out?
opts: A bacterial culture and sensitivity
That is used where the lesions appear secondarily infected.
Allergy patch testing of a standard series
That is considered in chronic or recurrent disease.
Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin
That investigates autoimmune blistering disease.
A potassium hydroxide preparation
Correct. Bacterial culture is added if lesions look secondarily infected.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Which dermoscopic findings support alopecia areata?
opts: Comedone-like openings and a stuck-on surface appearance
That is the dermoscopic appearance of seborrheic keratosis.
Yellow dots, black dots, broken hairs, tapered hairs and short regrowth
Correct — the diagnosis is clinical and dermoscopy strengthens it.
Finger-like projections with a moth-eaten border at the edge
That is the dermoscopic appearance of solar lentigo.
A dense dark head with the body, eggs and burrow trailing behind
That is the delta-wing jet sign in scabies.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: What terms describe complete scalp and complete body hair loss in alopecia areata?
opts: Androgenetic alopecia for scalp and alopecia totalis for body
Androgenetic alopecia is a separate condition.
Alopecia totalis for all scalp hair, alopecia universalis for all body hair
Correct.
Alopecia universalis for all scalp hair, alopecia totalis for all body hair
The terms are reversed.
Alopecia areata for scalp and alopecia diffusa for body
Neither term is used that way.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Where is minoxidil primarily effective?
opts: At the frontal hairline
Its effect is primarily at the crown.
Over the entire scalp equally
Its effect is regional.
Only in women
It is used in male-pattern hair loss, and its stated effect is at the crown.
In the crown region of the scalp
Correct — it prevents further loss and may produce regrowth, working best with finasteride.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: Nail clipping with periodic acid-Schiff stain evaluates which suspected condition?
opts: Onychomycosis
Correct.
Psoriatic nail disease
Nail changes occur in psoriasis but this stain targets fungal infection.
Subungual melanoma
That would require biopsy of the nail matrix.
Alopecia areata
Nail pitting occurs in alopecia areata, but this test is not how it is assessed.

set1.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set1.q: How are severe or extensive allergic contact dermatitis eruptions treated?
opts: A five-day course of oral corticosteroids without taper
Early discontinuation results in high rates of rebounding.
Oral antihistamines alone
Antihistamines address itch but are not the treatment for severe eruptions.
High-dose oral corticosteroids tapered over two to three weeks, because early discontinuation causes high rates of rebound
Correct. Limited eruptions can be managed with high-potency topical steroids.
High-potency topical steroids alone regardless of how extensive the eruption is across the body surface area
Topical therapy suits limited body surface area only.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What are the two primary clinical priorities in stasis dermatitis?
opts: Identifying the causative organism by culture and selecting an appropriate antibiotic
It is not an infectious condition.
Determining the allergen and arranging patch testing
That belongs to allergic contact dermatitis.
Staging the ulcer and measuring its depth
Ulceration is a complication rather than the stated priority.
Distinguishing it from cellulitis, and determining whether compression therapy can be used safely
Correct — both are named as the priorities.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the mechanism of pemphigus?
opts: Loss of keratinocyte-to-keratinocyte adhesion, called acantholysis, from autoantibodies to adhesion molecules, producing intraepithelial blisters
Correct — a life-threatening blistering disorder of skin and mucous membranes.
Autoimmune damage to the epithelial basement membrane producing subepithelial blistering that resolves without any scarring
That is bullous pemphigoid.
A type IV delayed hypersensitivity reaction to an external allergen
That is allergic contact dermatitis.
Impaired stratum-corneum hydration
That is xerosis.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does light microscopy show in bullous pemphigoid?
opts: Acantholysis
Acantholysis is the pemphigus finding.
Band-like infiltration of neutrophils throughout the papillary dermis
That is lichen planus.
Budding yeast and pseudohyphae
That indicates candidal infection.
Neutrophils aligned in a straight narrow row at the dermal-epidermal junction
Correct. Biopsy of a lesion goes for histopathology and perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence.

set2.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set2.q: How is a macule defined in this lecture?
opts: A flat elevated plateau lesion measuring greater than one centimetre across
That is a plaque.
A flat lesion less than one centimetre, without elevation or depression
Correct. A patch is the same lesion larger than one centimetre.
A flat lesion less than five millimetres
Five millimetres is the Clinical Pathophysiology convention; this course uses one centimetre.
An elevated solid lesion less than one centimetre
That is a papule.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is a positive Nikolsky sign?
opts: Lesions develop at sites of trauma
That is the Koebner phenomenon.
Fine white lacy lines appearing across the surface of the affected plaques
Those are Wickham's striae, seen in lichen planus.
The top layers of skin slip away or slough off from the lower layers when rubbed
Correct — positive in pemphigus, negative in bullous pemphigoid.
Removal of scale produces pinpoint bleeding
That is the Auspitz sign, seen in psoriasis.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: When should a lichen simplex chronicus plaque be biopsied?
opts: When the patient reports that the itch is worse at night than by day
Nocturnal itch is characteristic rather than a biopsy indication.
When emollients alone have failed to settle the plaque completely
Failure of emollients alone is not the stated trigger.
When it is atypical, unilateral, nodular, ulcerated or treatment-resistant
Correct — the purpose is to exclude neoplasia or another inflammatory disorder.
When it has been present for longer than six weeks in any location
Duration alone is not the stated trigger.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What are the four Ps of lichen planus?
opts: Pruritic, pustular, patchy plaques
That is not the mnemonic.
Purple, painless, peripheral pustular lesions
That is not the mnemonic.
Pruritic, purple, polygonal, papules or plaques
Correct — flat-topped, pink to violaceous and shiny, coalescing into larger plaques.
Painful, pale, punched-out papules
That is not the mnemonic.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is a dermatoscope used for?
opts: Magnified examination of a lesion's surface and pigment pattern
Correct — it is the first-line tool for evaluating a pigmented lesion.
Rapid bedside identification of a mite and its eggs in oil
That is the mineral oil preparation.
Detection of fungal elements after dissolving keratin in alkali
That is the potassium hydroxide preparation.
Measurement of the amount of viral genetic material present
That is what a quantitative molecular test measures.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How do urushiol lesions present, and over what time course?
opts: Diffuse urticarial wheals resolving within 24 hours
That describes urticaria.
Greasy scaling patches in sebum-rich areas over several weeks
That describes seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Intensely pruritic vesicular lesions in linear distributions, erupting within 4 to 96 hours and persisting up to 3 weeks
Correct — the linear pattern comes from grazing the plant in passing.
Well-demarcated plaques shaped like the object contacted, erupting within minutes of exposure and clearing within a day
That pattern fits metal, adhesive or jewellery allergy rather than urushiol.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which underlying process drives stasis dermatitis?
opts: Autoimmune destruction of the epidermal basement membrane
That describes bullous pemphigoid.
Chronic venous disease with lower-leg oedema
Correct — the dermatitis is a consequence of venous hypertension.
Chronic arterial insufficiency with reduced perfusion
Arterial disease matters here, but as a contraindication to compression.
Repeated contact with an environmental allergen
That produces allergic contact dermatitis.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is finasteride, and what are its cautions?
opts: An oral antiandrogen used first line in women
Finasteride is not indicated in women; oral antiandrogens such as combined oral contraceptives may be considered instead.
A topical 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor applied to the crown, whose effects on libido and erectile function are permanent and do not reverse at all when the drug is stopped
The effects are reversible when the drug is stopped.
An oral 5-alpha-reductase type 2 inhibitor; about 2% of men report reduced libido and erectile function, reversible on stopping, and it is not indicated in women and contraindicated in pregnancy
Correct, and it works best combined with minoxidil.
A topical vasodilator effective mainly at the crown
That describes minoxidil.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which comorbidities are patients with psoriasis at increased risk of?
opts: Cardiovascular events, type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic syndrome and lymphoma
Correct — psoriasis is a systemic inflammatory disease, not only a skin condition.
Chronic kidney disease, hepatic cirrhosis and early-onset osteoporosis
These are not the named associations.
Osteoporosis and vitamin D deficiency
These are not the named associations.
Asthma and allergic rhinitis
Those belong to the atopic triad.

set2.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set2.q: What distinguishes a plaque from a patch?
opts: A plaque is elevated and plateau-like; a patch is flat with no elevation
Correct — both exceed one centimetre, so elevation is the discriminator.
A plaque is larger than a patch
Both are greater than one centimetre; size does not separate them.
A plaque is fluid-filled and a patch is solid
Neither is fluid-filled.
A plaque is always poorly demarcated while a patch is always well demarcated
Demarcation is described separately and varies for both.

set2.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set2.q: What distinguishes an ulceration from an erosion?
opts: An ulceration is full-thickness loss extending to the dermis or deeper; an erosion loses only the epidermis
Correct — depth is the discriminator, and it determines whether the lesion can scar.
An ulceration is linear and an erosion is round
Shape does not distinguish them.
An ulceration is painful and an erosion is painless
Neither is defined by pain.
An ulceration involves only the epidermis and always heals without scarring, while an erosion reaches the dermis or deeper
The definitions are reversed.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What proportion of children worldwide are affected by atopic dermatitis, and in which sex is it more common?
opts: About 20% of children, more common in females
It is more common in males.
About 5% of children, more common in males
The figure given is 20%.
About 40% of children, with no sex difference
Neither figure nor the absence of a sex difference matches.
About 20% of children, more common in males
Correct. It often begins in infancy or childhood; adult-onset disease occurs but is rare.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the most common cause of allergic contact dermatitis, and roughly what proportion of people in the United States react to it?
opts: Perfumes and fragrance mixes — approximately 60% of people
Perfumes are a listed cause but not the most common.
Urushiol sap from Toxicodendron species — approximately 50 to 75%
Correct, which explains why not everyone who contacts poison ivy, sumac or oak reacts.
Nickel — approximately 90%
Nickel is the most common metal allergen but not the most common cause overall.
Neomycin — approximately 30%
Neomycin and bacitracin are common topical antibiotic causes but not the most common overall.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What underlies xerosis, and who is most affected?
opts: Impaired stratum-corneum hydration promoted by ageing, low humidity, hot water, detergents, atopy and systemic disease, commonly affecting older adults especially in winter
Correct, causing tightness, pruritus, rough scale, fissuring or eczema.
Overgrowth of Malassezia in sebum-rich areas, in young men
That is seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Chronic venous hypertension in the lower legs, in older adults
That is stasis dermatitis.
An autoimmune process affecting the epithelial basement membrane, occurring most often in the elderly and remitting spontaneously after five or six years
That is bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What is the most important modifiable association of perioral dermatitis?
opts: Topical corticosteroid exposure
Correct — and treatment begins by stopping it, with a warning that the eruption may temporarily worsen on withdrawal.
Sun exposure
Photoreactions are covered in General Dermatology II rather than being this association.
Overgrowth of Malassezia yeast
That is seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Nickel exposure
Nickel causes allergic contact dermatitis.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which three agents make up the medium to high potency tier?
opts: Betamethasone valerate 0.025%, tazarotene 0.1% and adapalene 0.1% preparations
The last two are retinoids rather than corticosteroids.
Triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, betamethasone valerate 0.1% and betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%
Correct. Betamethasone appears twice here, in two different salts.
Hydrocortisone 2.5%, betamethasone valerate 0.025% and clobetasol propionate 0.05%
Those are the mild, moderate and high agents respectively.
Triamcinolone acetonide 0.1%, hydrocortisone 1% and clobetasol propionate 0.05%
Hydrocortisone is mild and clobetasol is high.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which finding on a potassium hydroxide preparation supports candidal diaper dermatitis?
opts: Branching septate hyphae only
That pattern indicates a dermatophyte rather than Candida.
Multinucleated giant cells
That is the Tzanck smear finding in herpesvirus infection.
Mites, eggs or faecal pellets
That is the mineral oil preparation finding in scabies.
Budding yeast or pseudohyphae
Correct — fold involvement with satellite lesions is what prompts the test.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How does guttate psoriasis present, and what precedes it?
opts: Sudden generalised pustules with fever over the trunk and extremities
That is pustular psoriasis, the Von Zumbusch form.
Silvery plaques on the extensor elbows and knees
That is plaque psoriasis.
Erythematous patches with margins studded with subcorneal pustules, appearing typically during the third trimester of pregnancy
That is impetigo herpetiformis, psoriasis of pregnancy.
Raindrop-shaped erythematous papules and plaques in children, typically 2 to 3 weeks after a streptococcal infection or upper respiratory infection
Correct. It often needs no treatment, though phototherapy and topical steroids may be used.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which exposure most commonly precipitates perioral dermatitis?
opts: Repeated shaving of the beard area with a blade
That produces pseudofolliculitis barbae.
Topical corticosteroid applied to the face
Correct — continued exposure perpetuates it, so the steroid must be stopped.
Prolonged immersion of the hands in water
That predisposes to chronic paronychia and irritant dermatitis.
Occlusion of the skin under a plaster cast
That produces acne mechanica.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: What does a biopsy show in lichen planus?
opts: A band-like infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Correct — a classic descriptive phrase worth recognising on sight.
Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with junctional separation
That is Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis.
Granular immunoglobulin A deposits at the dermal papillae
That is dermatitis herpetiformis.
Subepidermal separation with linear immunoglobulin G at the basement membrane
That is bullous pemphigoid.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How are nummular eczema plaques described?
opts: Greasy yellow scaling plaques in sebum-rich areas
That describes seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Violaceous flat-topped polygonal papules with fine white lines
That describes lichen planus.
Intensely pruritic, round coin-shaped, light pink, scaly, thin plaques 1 to 10 cm, uniform without central clearing
Correct, most commonly on the extremities though they can occur on the trunk.
Well-demarcated salmon-pink plaques with prominent silvery scale on the extensor surfaces of the elbows and knees
That describes plaque psoriasis.

set2.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set2.q: What defines a wheal?
opts: A fluid-filled lesion containing leukocytes
That is a pustule.
A fluid-filled lesion under one centimetre
That is a vesicle.
A deposit of blood in the skin measuring one to two millimetres across
That is a petechia.
A firm oedematous plaque produced by infiltration of fluid into the dermis
Correct — the fluid is in the tissue rather than in a cavity, which is what separates it from a vesicle.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: Which supportive measure is described as one of the most important considerations in alopecia areata?
opts: Referral for hair transplantation early in the disease course
Transplantation is discussed for androgenetic rather than areata.
Referral to a wig service before starting any medical therapy
That is not what the lecture names.
Psychological support, with support groups offered
Correct — the visible nature of the condition carries real psychological weight.
Referral to endocrinology for thyroid function assessment
Autoimmune associations exist but this is not what is named here.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How can atopic dermatitis appear differently across skin tones?
opts: Violaceous on lighter skin, but hypopigmented on darker skin in every case
That is not how the difference is described.
Angry and inflamed on lighter skin, but almost silvery on darker skin
Correct — the underlying disease is the same but the visual signal is not.
Silvery on lighter skin, but angry and inflamed on darker skin
That reverses the two descriptions.
Identical on all skin tones, since the eruption is defined by its distribution
Distribution helps, but the appearance genuinely differs.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, manifestations, diagnosis and management of dermatological conditions
set2.q: How is pityriasis rosea treated?
opts: A tapering course of oral prednisone given over a period of two to three weeks from the outset of the eruption
That is used for severe allergic contact dermatitis.
Topical ketoconazole
That treats seborrhoeic dermatitis.
Oral doxycycline for six weeks
That is not the treatment for this condition.
It is self-limited, so reassurance is the mainstay, with antihistamines or topical steroids used cautiously for pruritus
Correct. Ultraviolet B phototherapy or sunlight helps if begun in the first week; severe cases may be treated with acyclovir.

set2.io: a — Anatomy of the integumentary system
set2.q: Which six features are used to translate a dermatological finding into words?
opts: Location, laterality, symmetry, tenderness, temperature and texture
These are not the six features named.
Primary morphology, secondary morphology, demarcation, colour, size and distribution
Correct. Getting all six into a description is what lets another provider picture the lesion without seeing it.
Primary morphology, colour and distribution only, since the rest are subjective
Demarcation, secondary morphology and size are all part of the description.
Onset, duration, severity, triggers, treatments tried and response
Those come from the history rather than the description of the lesion.

set2.io: c — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis of dermatological conditions
set2.q: A patient with bullous pemphigoid has not responded to prednisone and doxycycline. Which agents are used for refractory disease?
opts: Oral antihistamines and emollients while the disease burns itself out
Those do not control an autoimmune blistering disease.
Immunosuppressives such as methotrexate and azathioprine, with biologics and intravenous immunoglobulin also used
Correct — low-dose methotrexate is described as safe and effective in the elderly, with folic acid.
Ultrapotent topical corticosteroids applied to the whole of the skin surface twice daily for several weeks
Those are used for mild disease rather than for refractory disease.
Rituximab as the sole first-line agent, since it is used in pemphigus
Rituximab is the initial choice in pemphigus rather than here.
